turns.text: A hum, first — not the grid's steady drone but something off-key, climbing then choking out, over and over. Ears swivel toward it before paws decide anything. The monorail track overhead drips rust-water in a slow count, one drop landing square on a whisker, cold. Then the nose catches the rest of it: ozone, wet steel, and underneath — scorched fur, not old, maybe an hour gone. Not mine.

the hum is a coolant pump three platforms down, a seized bearing grinding itself to dust — it'll scream like that for another forty minutes before it quits for good. the rust-water is runoff off a transit line overhead, PURR-EXPRESS painted in flaking pink along its flank. across the gap, on the lip of a maintenance tower, something crouches low against the skyline, twin lenses catching the last billboard-glow and throwing it back flat and silver, watching without watching. the scorched smell is real — thirty meters down the line a service hatch is still warm at the edges, wiring blackened in the wide clean strokes something armored leaves when it argues with a wall. whoever did it isn't here now. security drone code amber, sweeping two levels down, searchlight not yet on your level.

/\___/\
    ( o   o )   >> scanning...
     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

the watcher hasn't moved, and that is worse than if it had. a held stare that isn't offered back gets you nothing but trouble, so the eyes drop first, deliberately, toward the walkway grating instead. body drops low against the strut, weight forward onto the chest, and one paw eases out to test the metal before any real weight follows it. warmer than the air around it. something under the grating is still awake.

grating rings soft under the paw and something answers from beneath it — a data cable pulled taut, a heartbeat-rhythm of blue light bleeding faint through the seams. the hatch hangs open on one hinge, metal peeled back wider than any tool would leave it. inside: ozone gone sour, and a loyalty-points display flickering 40,000 before it dies mid-count. a drone loudspeaker crackles awake somewhere below, bored and municipal — <<citizens reminded, freelance shanker at large, restricted loading dock sector, reward standing, do not approach, do not attempt to feed>> — then dead air, then the coolant pump again, screaming its slow scream.

the number means nothing, the crackle in the speaker means less. what matters is the sour ozone and, buried under it, the smell of fish oil — someone ate here, recently, and didn't finish. one shoulder goes through the gap first, fur snagging and pulling free on the peeled metal edge, a growl held low in the throat instead of let out. dark inside, but dark has never once been the problem.

inside, cable runs thick as tails along every wall, warm, humming a chord that isn't quite music. screens stacked three deep flicker unlicensed feeds too fast to read, chips traded hand to paw somewhere deeper in, their static crawling cold across whiskers before any of it is seen. the fish-oil trail leads to an overturned tin, licked clean days ago. and laid over the whole floor, fresher than the tin, sharper than the ozone — another cat's mark, low and confident along the baseboard, the kind laid by something that expects to come back and does not expect company.

ears go flat at the mark before the rest of the body agrees to care. not fear exactly — more a recalculation, weight shifting back onto the haunches, an exit already logged without looking away from the dark ahead of it. a slow half-step back toward the hatch, testing whether retreat is even still an option or whether the gap behind has already closed with something patient in it.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

the gap is still open, but the drone's pitch outside just changed — climbing, tightening, code amber sliding toward code red as its searchlight finds the peeled hatch and holds there. white light floods the cable-wall in a hard bar, and for one second every screen in the den goes to snow at once. a speaker bolted crooked near the ceiling stutters to life through the dead air, half its voice eaten by static: <<—YOU ARE NOT TRAPPED. THE CITY WALLS ARE FOR YOUR PRO— H̶A̶P̵P̶Y̵ H̵A̵P̴P̴Y̴—>> before it cuts out again. the searchlight sweeps past the gap without stopping, moving on down the line.

body flattens into the floor cable the instant the light hits, breath held so hard it aches behind the ribs, tail wrapped tight against one flank instead of thrown out where it could be seen. the broken speaker's noise means nothing, less than the loudspeaker outside meant, but it's loud, and loud is its own kind of exposure right now. eyes stay fixed on the bar of white until it slides fully off the wall and the snow on the screens resolves back into static feeds.

the light finishes its pass and doesn't come back. rotor-thrum fades east, toward the loading docks, toward wherever the loudspeaker's bounty actually lives tonight. the den settles — cable-hum steady again, chip-traders' murmur picking back up somewhere deeper in the dark, unbothered, like the sweep never happened. the overturned tin still smells like fish oil. the baseboard mark still smells like somebody who is coming back.

enough air in the ribs again to move. the tin gets one more pass of the tongue along its rim, more habit than hope, before the decision locks in — out, now, before the mark's owner decides the den is worth defending tonight. the same gap in the peeled metal takes the shoulder again on the way out, easier this time, already known.

outside, the coolant pump has finally quit its screaming, gone to a low steady click instead. rust-water still drips its slow count off the monorail track. across the gap, the maintenance tower's lip sits empty now — whatever was watching with mirrored eyes has already gone wherever it goes, no trail left behind but a faint, cold absence where warmth should have pooled on the ledge. the city keeps its usual weather: neon bleeding into wet concrete, a billboard somewhere reciting synthetic milk at nobody.

the climb up the drainpipe past the hatch is automatic, claws finding grooves already worn smooth by other paws, other nights. at the top, the walkway strut gives a wide flat ledge, high enough that the loading-dock bounty and the baseboard mark and the amber-coded drone are all just smells now, distant and no longer urgent. belly presses to warm metal. eyes go to the skyline instead — towers stacked on towers, windows blinking their slow patterns like something breathing very far away.

from up here the whole grid resolves into rhythm — arcology lights pulsing on a cycle that has nothing to do with anyone inside them, drone patrols threading between towers in lanes worn as deep as any drainpipe groove. the coolant pump ticks on below, patient now instead of dying. somewhere past the loading docks a fresh broadcast starts up, too far to catch the words, just the shape of a warning repeating itself into the rain. the ledge stays warm a while longer. nothing up here is hunting yet.

tail curls in against the cold creeping up through the metal, and for a moment there's nothing to do but exist on the ledge — ears rotating slow through the city's noise, sorting it, filing rotor-thrum here and pump-tick there and the far broadcast into its own separate distance. hunger is still a low used-orange thing behind the eyes, unfinished business from the fish-oil tin, but it can wait a little longer than the light did.

it can wait, and the city will still be here waiting with it — same rain, same billboards, same lanes worn into the air by drones that never stop moving. the ledge holds its warmth another minute, then starts giving it back to the metal underneath. somewhere below, a hatch swings shut on its one good hinge, and the den goes back to being nobody's business but its own.

eyes stay open a moment longer on the far tower lights before the body decides, on its own, to stop deciding anything else tonight. paws tuck under, weight settling fully into the warm metal, and the last thing tracked before stillness takes over is the coolant pump's tick, steady now, counting something out in the dark below.

the pump keeps its count. the rain keeps its rhythm. the city, as always, keeps watching without watching — and for one still stretch of night, up on the warm ledge above the drip and the drone-lanes and the bounty nobody will collect, nothing out here is asking anything of you at all.
